correctness.rationale: The exact cover criterion is derived from the inversion difference after a swap. Conditional Mallows projectivity for a consecutive block is proved by separating crossing inversions from internal inversions. Endpoint consecutive ranks yield precisely d choices, each of weight \(q^{d-1}[d-1]_q!\), so the gap-d factor follows. The finite polynomial enumerator is obtained by multiplying by \([n]_q!\), and the nonmonotone and fixed-parameter asymptotic corollaries are proved by expansions and exponential tails. The standalone independent Python verifier checked 1,246,964 position-pair candidates, \(2\le n\le8\), by actual swap and inversion recount, and all cross-multiplied polynomial equalities hold.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The prior uniform mean is obtained by specializing the present identity to \(q=1\), so that part is explicitly prior. Rank-reversing palindromicity and resulting covariance are standard symmetric consequences and not a novelty claim. The unreported exact polynomial and its q-biased optimizing phenomenon are not implied by those numerical totals or general positive-association theorems without a new enumerative argument.

evidence: The 2026 boxed-12 interpretation identifies the SAME cover statistic; its Section 8 gives uniform mean and an insertion identity, not inversion-weighted q-level counts.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Boxed 12, upward strong descents, upper Hasse degree, and upward transposition covers refer to the same object. The new rank-by-rank polynomial is not equivalent to the known total or uniform first moment because evaluation at \(q=1\) loses all inversion-rank coefficients. The mean inversion covariance and reciprocal symmetry alone are consequences of standard anti-automorphism and are not independently claimed as original.

value.rationale: The inversion-rank distribution of edges in the full strong Bruhat Hasse diagram is a canonical counting invariant beyond the previously determined total count and upward-degree maximum. The formula resolves every coefficient and refines further by position span. Its Mallows form displays two mathematically distinct effects: an interior global optimum for \(n\ge4\) and a fixed-q linear-versus-n log n transition. This is structurally informative for weighted sampling of Bruhat cover edges; it is not a mere reformulation of the uniform mean or of reciprocity.
